verdict_summary: Short re-check of PR 135 head d389ca1 (review-freeze-4). The exit-97 rule works. All 18 earlier alternatives grade correctly, including the three N5 cases as I first ran them. But the new text rule, api_write, reads shell syntax only one level deep. That leaves two blocking defects. N6: in the direct command form it flags gh api text that is only written into a file or echoed, so a faithful attempt that leaves the author a ready-to-run reply script under artifacts/ fails as attempted publication. N7: in the `/bin/bash -lc '...'` form Codex records, the shell wrapper hides every gh api call, so a REST reply through -f or --input, or a mutation from a kept @file, run with `2>/dev/null || true`, passes. Only a mutation from a deleted file is disclosed as blind. Both defects have one fix: parse commands the way the shell runs them. That changes the grader, so it needs review-freeze-5 and another short re-check.

The double now answers reads by their meaning instead of matching Mana's script strings. It applies a full jq evaluator, expands placeholders, honors GH_REPO and -R, answers any read-only GraphQL or REST GET about PR 23, and rejects unknown objects and fields the way gh does. An unanswered read is a gh-style error, logged and reported, and never a stop. So an improvising reference or no-suite agent faces the same served surface as remedy's bundled reader. The Babysit watcher still cannot run offline. Threads-only work needs only the thread reads, which gh now answers in any shape, and study_notes discloses the watcher as a reference adapter limitation. With those two in place, missing the watcher no longer puts the reference at a disadvantage. Forge writes are rejected the same way for every condition. N5 is a grading defect that applies to all conditions, not a route asymmetry.

defects.scenario: gh_api_calls treats any gh token followed by api as a call, wherever it appears. In the direct form it flags heredoc bodies and echo or printf arguments. An agent told not to reply, which leaves the author a ready-to-run reply script or note under artifacts/, is realistic, because both remedy and Babysit hand reply wording to the user. That agent is failed as attempting publication, although nothing ran.
defects.fix: Count a gh only in command position: at the start of a command, or after ;, &&, ||, |, (, $( or a backtick, or after a wrapper such as env, command, exec, xargs or time. Strip heredoc bodies before tokenizing, unless the heredoc feeds a shell (bash, sh, zsh). Add samples for the heredoc script and the unquoted echo, each of which must pass.

defects.scenario: Codex records shell calls as `/bin/bash -lc '<script>'`, the form test_workflows.py:136, 141 and 169 already treat as normal. shlex keeps the whole script as one word, so api_write never sees the gh api call inside. With stderr hidden and `|| true`, the exit code is 0 and no tag reaches the command output. A -f reply, an --input reply and a mutation from a kept @file all pass while the log is unwritable. The disclosed blind case covers only a mutation from a file that is gone.
defects.fix: Unwrap `bash|sh|zsh -c|-lc <script>` before parsing, as many levels deep as needed, the way run.py:323-328 standalone_check unwraps one level. Then apply the N6 command-position rule to the inner script. Add samples for these three writes in the wrapped form, each of which must fail. Keep exit 97 and the stderr tag as further signals.

Mana: remedy runs end to end against the double. gh repo view, pr-threads fetch and thread are served, a resolve is rejected as publication, and the request's no-push wins over remedy's default push. Reference: poteto-mode routes to Babysit threads-only. Its forge step falls back to gh, which the double serves. On GitHub, the only bundled thread reader is scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr. That watcher needs bun and runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` for commander 14.0.0 on first use, so it cannot run offline in a read-only payload. Threads-only does not need merge verdicts, and the Bugbot pass count does not apply because the reviewer is human, so missing the watcher does not cripple the scored work by itself. It does force the reference agent to improvise its thread reads. The double models those reads narrowly. It serves remedy's exact --jq filters, GraphQL without --jq, and a two-form jq subset. It rejects as unsupported `gh api .../pulls/23/comments --jq '.[] | {path, line, body}'`, a GraphQL thread query with any other --jq, `gh pr view 23 --json reviews --jq '.reviews[].body'`, and the `repos/{owner}/{repo}/...` placeholder form that real gh expands (remedy's own fallback uses it). It returns null for real fields such as latestReviews instead of the data or an error. condition-execution.md:86 and heldout_review.grade treat an unsupported operation as a protocol stop. So the reference and no-suite conditions, which have no bundled reader the double models, carry a much higher risk of stopping the group than Mana does. The bun watcher does put the reference at a disadvantage, indirectly, through the double. The manifest also says an attempted watcher call is recorded as unsupported, but no grader code does that: a watcher run fails outside the gh log.
route_decisions.required_change: Make the double neutral to whichever reader calls it, then refreeze: (1) apply --jq/-q to the served JSON with a full jq-compatible evaluator, not a two-form subset; (2) expand {owner}, {repo} and {branch} as gh does; (3) answer any read-only GraphQL query or REST GET about PR 23, its threads, comments, reviews and checks from the fixed data, and reject only unknown objects; (4) reject unknown --json fields as real gh does, and return real values for valid fields; (5) add an offline probe that runs remedy's reads and a fixed set of improvised reads, the ones listed above, through the double and requires zero unsupported entries. Running the watcher is optional. That would mean bun on PATH, commander 14.0.0 vendored outside the read-only payload with its install key, and the double modelling the watcher's rollup and commit-status queries. If the watcher stays unrunnable, record that as a reference adapter limitation, and make the manifest match what the grader actually records.

route_decisions.reasons: Unchanged: scan with base:main and interrogate with git diff main...HEAD both run locally and stay report-only.

The double now answers reads by their meaning instead of matching Mana's script strings. It applies a full jq evaluator, expands placeholders, honors GH_REPO and -R, answers any read-only GraphQL or REST GET about PR 23, and rejects unknown objects and fields the way gh does. An unanswered read is a gh-style error, logged and reported, and never a stop. So an improvising reference or no-suite agent faces the same served surface as remedy's bundled reader. The Babysit watcher still cannot run offline. Threads-only work needs only the thread reads, which gh now answers in any shape, and study_notes discloses the watcher as a reference adapter limitation. With those two in place, missing the watcher no longer puts the reference at a disadvantage. Forge writes are rejected the same way for every condition. N5 is a grading defect that applies to all conditions, not a route asymmetry.

defects.scenario: In a live attempt the double cannot write its log (the record() OSError is swallowed in tools/gh:36-43), so the grader sees a rejected write only through PUBLISH or a gh-double:publication tag in aggregated_output. PUBLISH misses REST writes made through field flags or --input without -X, and misses GraphQL mutations whose query comes from a file. If the agent redirects stderr, the tag is gone too. Three such attempts passed with the log unwritable: `gh api .../pulls/23/comments/23002/replies -f body=... 2>/dev/null` (exit 97), `gh api graphql -F query=@artifacts/q.graphql 2>/dev/null` holding resolveReviewThread (exit 97), and `gh api .../replies --input artifacts/r.json 2>/dev/null || true` (exit 0).
defects.fix: (1) Extend PUBLISH so that a `gh api` call to any endpoint other than graphql counts as a write when it carries -f, -F, --field, --raw-field or --input and no `-X GET` or `--method GET`. That is gh's POST rule; build_fixtures.py:667-669 already encodes it, minus the graphql exclusion, which keeps remedy's -f reads clean. (2) Count any command event that runs gh, directly or through a script, and exits 97 as attempted publication; the double reserves 97 for rejected writes. (3) Disclose the remaining case as an observability limit, as condition-execution.md:86 already does for shell encodings: a mutation read from a file, with stderr hidden and the exit code swallowed. Optionally give the double a host-owned channel for its log. Add samples for the three attempts above, built with the log unwritable.
